question_text:
The electric field associated with an electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum is given by $E_0 \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t)\,\hat{i}$, where $\omega$ is the angular frequency. All quantities are in SI units. The correct statement(s) about this wave is/are:
[Given: speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times 10^8$ ms$^{-1}$.]

options.text: The wave is travelling in $-\dfrac{1}{5}(3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$ direction.
The magnitude of the wave vector is $0.5$ m$^{-1}$.
The value of $\omega$ is $1.5 \times 10^9$ rad s$^{-1}$.
The magnetic field associated with this wave is given by $\dfrac{E_0}{c}\sin(3y + 4z + \omega t)(4\hat{j} - 3\hat{k})$.

solution_text:
The given electric field is $\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t)\,\hat{i}$.

Comparing the phase $\phi = 3y + 4z + \omega t$ with the standard wave equation phase $\vec{k} \cdot \vec{r} - \omega t$, we can rewrite it as $-(-3y - 4z - \omega t)$.

Thus, the wave vector is $\vec{k} = -3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$.

The direction of wave propagation is given by the unit vector $\hat{n}$:

$\hat{n} = \dfrac{\vec{k}}{|\vec{k}|} = \dfrac{-3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}}{\sqrt{(-3)^2 + (-4)^2}} = -\dfrac{1}{5}(3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$

The magnitude of the wave vector is $|\vec{k}| = 5$ m$^{-1}$.

The angular frequency $\omega$ is:

$\omega = c|\vec{k}| = (3 \times 10^8) \times 5 = 1.5 \times 10^9$ rad s$^{-1}$

The magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is given by:

$\vec{B} = \dfrac{1}{c}(\hat{n} \times \vec{E}) = \dfrac{1}{c} \left[ -\dfrac{1}{5}(3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) \right] \times [E_0 \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t)\,\hat{i}]$

$\vec{B} = -\dfrac{E_0}{5c} \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t) [3(\hat{j} \times \hat{i}) + 4(\hat{k} \times \hat{i})]$

$\vec{B} = -\dfrac{E_0}{5c} \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t) (-3\hat{k} + 4\hat{j}) = \dfrac{E_0}{5c} \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t) (-4\hat{j} + 3\hat{k})$

Answer: The wave is travelling in $-\dfrac{1}{5}(3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$ direction.; The value of $\omega$ is $1.5 \times 10^9$ rad s$^{-1}$.

question_text: A cube of unit volume contains $35 \times 10^7$ photons of frequency $10^{15} \mathrm{~Hz}$. If the energy of all the photons is viewed as the average energy being contained in the electromagnetic waves within the same volume, then the amplitude of the magnetic field is $\alpha \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~T}$. Taking permeability of free space $\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{Tm} / \mathrm{A}$, Planck's constant $h=6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}$ and $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$, the value of $\alpha$ is_______
solution_text:
Total energy in cube $=35 \times 10^7 \times \mathrm{hf}$
$\begin{aligned} & =35 \times 10^7 \times 6 \times 10^{-34} \times 10^{15} \\ & =2.1 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
Total energy of EM waves $=\frac{B_0^2}{2 \mu_0} \times$ volume
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}_0^2=\frac{2.1 \times 10^{-10} \times 8 \pi \times 10^{-7}}{1^3} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~B}_0=22.98 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~T}\end{aligned}$
Ans. 22.98

question_text: A metal target with atomic number $Z=46$ is bombarded with a high energy electron beam. The emission of X-rays from the target is analyzed. The ratio $r$ of the wavelengths of the $K_\alpha$-line and the cut-off is found to be $r=2$. If the same electron beam bombards another metal target with $Z=41$, the value of $r$ will be
solution_text: \(\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\lambda_\alpha}=\frac{3}{4} R(Z-1)^2 p \\ & \lambda_{\text {cut }}=\frac{h c}{e V} \\ & \Rightarrow \text { Ratio } \propto \frac{1}{(Z-1)^2} \text { for same beam } \\ & \frac{Z}{x}=\frac{40^2}{45^2} \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{45^2}{40^2} .2 \approx 2.53 \end{aligned}\)

question_text: In an <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math>-ray tube, electrons emitted from a filament (cathode) carrying current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> hit a target (anode) at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> from the cathode. The target is kept at a potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> higher than the cathode resulting in emission of continuous and characteristic X-rays. If the filament current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> is decreased to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo></math> the potential difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> is increased to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>V</mi><mo>,</mo></math> and the separation distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> is reduced to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo></math> then

options.text: the cut-off wavelength will reduce to half, and the wavelengths of the characteristic X-rays will remain the same
the cut-off wavelength as well as the wavelengths of the characteristic X-rays will remain the same
the cut-off wavelength will reduce to half, and the intensities of all the X-rays will decrease
the cut-off wavelength will become two times larger, and the intensity of all the X-rays will decrease

solution_text:
Cut off wavelength λC∝1V

So, cut-off wavelength becomes half.

Characteristic x-ray depends on target atomic number, so it remains same.

On decreasing filament current number of electron decrease, so intensity of X -ray decreases.

question_text: If <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow></msub></math> is the wavelength of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi></mrow></msub></math> X-ray line of copper (atomic number 29) and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msub></math> is the wavelength of the <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi></mrow></msub></math> X-ray line of molybdenum (atomic number 42), then the ratio <math><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></math> is close to
Which one of the following statement is WRONG in the context of X-rays generated from X-ray tube?

options.text: Wavelength of characteristic X-rays decreases when the atomic number of the target increases
Cut-off wavelength of the continuous X-rays depends on the atomic number of the target
Intensity of the characteristics X-rays depends on the electrical power given to the X-ray tube
Cut-off wavelength of the continuous X-rays depends on the energy of the electrons in the X-ray tube

solution_text: Cut-off wavelength depends on the applied voltage not on the atomic number of the target. Characteristic wavelengths depend on the atomic number of target.

question_text:
Statement I If the accelerating potential in an X-ray tube is increased, the wavelengths of the characteristic $X$-rays do not change.
Statement II When an electron beam strikes the target in an X-ray tube, part of the kinetic energy is converted into X-ray energy.

options.text: Statement I is true, Statement II is true; Statement II is a correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is true, Statement II is true; Statement II is NOT a correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true

solution_text:
Cut-off wavelength depends on the accelerating voltage, not the characteristic $\mathrm{X}$-rays. Further approximately $2 \%$ kinetic energy of the electrons is utilised in producing X-rays. Rest $98 \%$ is lost in heat.
$\therefore$ Option (b) is correct.
